newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Tuesday, Feb 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Tuesday, Feb 18.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- POUND HITS UK CAR PART SALES

A senior purchasing executive at Volkswagen, the German automotive giant, has said the continuing strength of sterling is making Britain's motor components industry uncompetitive. Frans Boot, head of VW's purchasing in the UK and Scandinavia, said the British car parts industry is losing millions of pounds in potential business from VW because of the high pound. The warning was echoed by Walter Hasselkus, head of Rover, who said the company was considering buying more parts abroad.
-- VW AND GM REPLY CAUTIOUSLY TO BRIBERY ALLEGATIONS

Automotive giants Volkswagen and General Motors have both issued cautious responses to claims in the German magazine Der Spiegel that members of their purchasing staffs had been extorting bribes from suppliers seeking contracts. VW, Europe's biggest carmaker, said on Monday it had asked German prosecutors to investigate bribery allegations relating to a new paint plant at its Czech subsidiary Skoda. GM, whose Adam Opel German subsidiary was implicated in the article, said it was doing 'exactly as you would expect any responsible company to do'.
-- WATCHDOG MOVES AGAINST OFF-BALANCE SHEET SCHEMES

The Financial Reporting Review Panel, an investigative sister body of the Accounting Standards Board, has indicated to listed companies that they could face a crackdown on creative accounting. The FRRP moved after agreeing with Associated Nursing Services, the long-term care provider, that its accounts should be amended because of the way a sale and lease-back transaction was reported in the accounts. The move has implications for hundreds of companies in the UK that employ such sale and lease-back transactions.
-- GERMANY FACES SPENDING CURB TO MEET EMU TARGET

Germany's deputy finance minister, Jurgen Stark, has told a meeting of European Union finance ministers his country is ready to adopt emergency measures to meet this year's budget deficit target for European economic and monetary union. He said Germany was ready to impose a spending freeze to combat a shortfall in tax revenues caused by the country's record unemployment.
-- MEDICAL INSURANCE TAX LOOPHOLE TO BE CLOSED

Customs and Excise is to close a tax loophole that has been exploited by heathcare company PPP to create the fastest growing private medical insurance package in the market. PPP has been marketing the product on the basis of its exemption from a four percent insurance premium which applies to annually renewable private health cover. By fixing the administration fee for the first three of the five years of guaranteed cover, the PPP product was exempt from the levy.
-- LONDON CLUBS IN 178 MILLION STG BID FOR RIVAL CASINO GROUP

Casino group London Clubs International has launched a 178 million stg hostile bid for Capital Corp, the group that runs the London casinos Crockfords and the Colony Club. If successful the bid would give London Clubs, operator of the Ritz and Les Ambassadeurs, up to 60 percent of the London casino market. The bid follows a profit warning from Capital, which said that 1996 pre-tax profits could be up to 35 percent below expectations.
-- SHANDWICK DIRECTORS QUIT TO LAUNCH RIVAL

In a move recalling the heady days of the 1980s, four board directors and one assistant director at public relations group Shandwick Consultants are expected to announce Tuesday they are leaving to set up a rival company. The executives are thought to include directors handling public relations for Halifax building society, 3i venture capitalists and British Gas.
-- GULF EDGES CLOSER TO SUCCESS IN BID BATTLE FOR CLYDE

Analysts expect Gulf Canada Resources to be successful in its 494-million-stg hostile takeover bid for UK oil independent Clyde Petroleum. Gulf enters the final day of the bid, Tuesday, with almost 41 percent of the shares in its target after it received acceptances from holders of 10.98 percent of the shares in Clyde. The bid is likely to be close, with one of Clyde's institutional investors expected to determine the final outcome.
-- PROFIT-TAKING HITS CENTRICA SHARES

Shares in Centrica, the former supply and trading arm of British Gas, fell 10.25p to close at 65.25p on Monday, the first day of they traded on the stock market. Dealers said the stock was hit by profit-taking after a week of steady gains in the 'gray market' and concerns about the company's competitiveness in the UK domestic gas market as it is opened to competition.
-- TELEFONICA SELL-OFF BEATS EXPECTATIONS

Telefonica, Spain's national telecoms group, has described its privatisation as 'extraordinarily successful'. The sale of the remaining 21 percent of state-owned equity, which was completed on Monday, raised some Pta650 billion ($4.6 billion). Shares in Telefonica will commence trading on Tuesday.
